references.text: God's original command to collect gifts of silver, copper, and acacia wood for the tabernacle
Moses' appeal to the people to bring offerings to the Lord's sanctuary, including silver, copper, and acacia wood
The people continue bringing voluntary gifts for the construction of the tabernacle
Overview of the copper given as an offering and used for the tabernacle
The tribal leaders bring silver bowls and other offerings to the sanctuary
David's appeal for voluntary gifts of precious metals for the temple, parallel to the collection for the tabernacle
Paul teaches about willing generosity based on what one has, reflecting the principle of voluntary giving in Exodus
Both verses belong to the same event concerning the collection of materials for the tabernacle and emphasize the principle of voluntary giving.
A strong theological parallel showing how the principle of voluntary giving to God's house is repeated from the tabernacle (Exodus) to the temple (Chronicles).
David repeats exactly the same list of materials as in Exodus to build God's house, underscoring the continuity of the giving principle.
